audit_plan.report:
## Claim being audited

This is the cycle-5 coverage re-plan for the five configured targets that still have no covering node. The first four tasks of the prior plan are complete: the increasing-embedding/local-constancy foundation, generalized-shift reduction and consequences, and the front/Nash-Williams/SuperNW statement package are present. Their configured targets are covered and should not be reconstructed. The current node-level correspondence, substantiveness, and soundness findings on that already-built material are separate verifier work; this coverage plan uses the principal statements and follows the reviewer's instruction not to rewrite them during the next construction burst.

The remaining targets are exactly `lem:subarr`, `lines:985-987`, `cor PowerQPresBqo`, `thm BqoHerCtblWqo`, and `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. The four still-live tasks from the prior plan remain mathematically correct, but they now need sharper attachment points and smaller support packages.

## Existing interfaces and one correction

`IncSeq`, `RightComp`, `ShiftMap`, `LocallyConstant`, `BadMultiSequence`, and `Bqo` provide the multi-sequence side. `Front`, `FrontRestrict`, `SuperSequence`, `NashWilliams`, and `SuperNW` provide the front side. The probe at `.trellis/stuck-math-audit/cycle-5-request-33/right_comp_probe.lean` confirms on the nontrivial embedding `n |-> 2*n` that `ShiftMap x` evaluates as `x (n+1)`, so the existing shift interface can be reused.

There is, however, an orientation issue relevant to the later hereditary-countability construction. The current Lean signature of `FrontTreeWellFounded` makes `u` related to `v` when `u` is a proper initial segment of `v`. In Lean's `WellFounded r` recursion, computing at `s` may call values at `t` when `r t s`; the paper's definition of `TildeF(s)` at lines 1559-1563 calls `TildeF(t)` for strict extensions `t` of `s`. Thus that construction needs the converse relation, `r child parent` iff `parent` is a proper initial segment of `child`. Add a correctly oriented helper for this use; do not pretend the current signature supplies the recursion principle. This does not require changing the already covered Nash-Williams statement during the next burst.

## Remaining DAG

```text
Front + SuperSequence + ProperPrefixSet
  + IncSeq/RightComp + LocallyConstant
    -> unique front selector / super extension
    -> minimal deciding front / multi restriction
    -> finite shift and bad/perfect transports
    + NashWilliams -> shift perfect-or-bad dichotomy -> Subarr

NashWilliams -> constant-k front Ramsey (k=3,4)
  + Rado order + domination on Set Q
  + bad-powerset witness map -> two thinnings -> RadoEmbedding

PowerTree(atom, arbitrary nonempty indexed node)
  -> support + four-clause PowerRel + preorder/extensional invariance
  -> finite comparison strategies and canonical negative moves
  + LocallyConstant/BadMultiSequence -> BadMapReflection
  + Bqo -> PowerQPresBqo

PowerTree + HereditarilyCountable
  + correctly oriented front-extension well-foundedness
  + bad multi-to-super transport -> TildeF -> ConverseGame
  + PowerQPresBqo + Bqo-to-Wqo -> BqoHerCtblWqo
  + countable tail-node construction -> BqoHerCtblWellF
```

For `lem:subarr`, represent a sub-multi-sequence of `h` by precomposition with `RightComp z`. Prove its commutation with `ShiftMap`, preservation of local constancy, and preservation of badness. For a super-sequence on an arbitrary front base `X`, select the unique front member properly prefixing an increasing enumeration whose range lies in `X`; reindex through an increasing enumeration of `X` when a global `MultiSequence` is required. The minimal deciding-front construction of paper lines 1277-1289 then makes the Boolean coloring `r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x))` into a super-sequence. `NashWilliams` yields a restriction on which this coloring is constant, hence a perfect-or-bad dichotomy. The target node must state all three equivalent clauses at paper lines 1652-1658 and prove every implication, including both badness transports and perfectness under restriction.

For `lines:985-987`, use a first-level domination relation on `Set Q`; this is intentionally separate from the iterated hierarchy. Define Rado pairs with `m<n` and the two-clause Rado order. From failure of wqo for domination, choose the bad pair-indexed witness map from paper lines 957-980. Obtain the homogeneous triple and quadruple sets from `NashWilliams` applied to constant-cardinality fronts, as required by process memory pm-0003. The final theorem assumes that `r` is a quasi-order and wqo, and produces a relation embedding of Rado's order into `r`. Its proof must establish both preservation and reflection; the three reflection cases at paper line 993 use badness and transitivity and may not be replaced by monotonicity alone.

For `cor PowerQPresBqo`, retain process memory pm-0002. The carrier must be a universe-polymorphic well-founded tree/preset type with an atom constructor for `Q` and a constructor for an arbitrary nonempty indexed family of earlier trees. Define the lifted relation by all four cases at paper lines 1404-1419, including the often-omitted set-to-atom universal clause. Raw presentations are acceptable only after proving that duplicate/extensional presentations are mutually related and that all predicates used by the targets are invariant under that equivalence. The comparison game, or an equivalent inductively defined negative strategy, must expose the existential Player-I choices supplied by `not PowerRel`. Canonicalize choices as functions of the compared tree values: choosing unrelated strategies separately for each input `x` would not prove that the reflected atom map is locally constant. The reflection node must match lines 1533-1550: every bad locally constant map into the full hierarchy yields a bad locally constant atom-valued map whose value lies in the source support. `PowerQPresBqo` is then the immediate contradiction with `Bqo r`.

For the hereditary targets, define hereditary countability recursively: atoms qualify, and a node qualifies exactly when its index type is countable and every child qualifies. Prove closure under nonempty countable families and induced-subtype inheritance. The reverse direction of `thm BqoHerCtblWqo` uses the bad multi-to-super bridge, the correctly oriented front recursion to build `TildeF`, and the comparison-game copying lemma `ConverseGame`; every internal node of `TildeF` is indexed by a subset of `Nat`, hence is hereditarily countable. The forward direction uses `PowerQPresBqo`, restriction to the hereditary subtype, and the elementary theorem that bqo implies wqo.

Finally, `thm BqoHerCtblWellF` must use the special closure of this hierarchy, not the false general assertion that a well-founded quasi-order is wqo. Wqo implies well-foundedness of the strict part. Conversely, from a bad sequence `(a_n)` in the hereditary hierarchy, form the nonempty countable tail nodes `A_n = {a_k | n <= k}`. Then `A_(n+1) <= A_n`, while `A_n <= A_(n+1)` would compare `a_n` with some later `a_k`, contradicting badness. These tail nodes give a strict descending chain inside the same hereditary hierarchy.

## Work order

Proceed in this order: (1) the super/multi bridge and `Subarr`; (2) constant-arity Ramsey support and the Rado embedding; (3) the iterated hierarchy core and bad-map reflection, then `PowerQPresBqo`; (4) hereditary countability, `TildeF`, and `ConverseGame`; (5) the wqo and well-founded hereditary characterizations. Each helper is its own paired node, dependencies cite principal declarations only, and every new proof-bearing TeX node must contain a complete proof rather than `SKETCH:`.

tasks.title: Build the super/multi bridge
tasks.body: Attach to `Front`, `FrontRestrict`, `SuperSequence`, `ProperPrefixSet`, `IncSeq`, `RightComp`, `ShiftMap`, and `LocallyConstant`. Add separate nodes for existence and uniqueness of the front prefix of an increasing enumeration, extension of a super-sequence to enumerations of its arbitrary base, restriction of a multi-sequence by `RightComp`, commutation of restriction with shift, and preservation of local constancy. Define the deciding-prefix set and prove that its initial-segment-minimal members form the front of paper lines 1277-1289, with the induced value map reconstructing the original multi-sequence. Define the finite-set shift relation from lines 1465-1468. Prove badness transport from multi to deciding super, from super to its extension, and under restriction; also prove the corresponding perfectness restriction/extension facts. Do not specialize fronts to fixed cardinality or silently replace an arbitrary base by `Set.univ`.

tasks.title: Prove the subarr equivalence
tasks.body: Carry forward the prior live task, now downstream of `super-multi-bridge-support`. Define perfect multi-sequences and perfect super-sequences for an arbitrary relation. Prove that `x |-> decide (r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x)))` is locally constant when `h` is, convert it through the deciding front, and apply `NashWilliams` to obtain a restricted multi-sequence that is either perfect or bad. State one target-covering theorem for `lem:subarr` with an explicit quasi-order hypothesis and exactly the three clauses: `Bqo r`; every locally constant multi-sequence has a perfect restriction; every super-sequence on any front/base has a perfect restricted sub-super-sequence. Give complete proofs of all implications, using the badness and perfectness transports rather than only the implication printed at paper lines 1660-1662.

tasks.title: Build Rado and Ramsey support
tasks.body: Attach to `NashWilliams`. Define the carrier of increasing natural pairs, Rado's two-clause partial order, first-level domination on `Set Q`, and relation embeddings. Add the witness-selection equivalence between a bad domination sequence and a bad map on increasing pairs. Prove that the family of `k`-element subsets of an infinite base is a front for positive `k`, then derive the binary homogeneous triple and quadruple lemmas by applying `NashWilliams` to the `k=3` and `k=4` fronts. This is the only Ramsey infrastructure needed; do not start an independent infinite Ramsey development.

tasks.title: Cover the Rado embedding target
tasks.body: Carry forward the prior task downstream of `rado-ramsey-support`. For a relation `r` with an explicit quasi-order structure, assume `WellQuasiOrdered r` and failure of wqo for domination on `Set Q`. Extract the bad pair map, thin first on triples to force `f(i,j) r f(i,k)`, and then on quadruples to force `f(i,j) r f(k,l)` for `i<j<k<l`; rule out the opposite colors using wqo. Reindex the final infinite set by an `IncSeq` and define the Rado map. Prove preservation and all reflection cases from paper line 993, hence injectivity and a genuine relation embedding. The final node alone claims `lines:985-987`.

tasks.title: Define the full iterated hierarchy
tasks.body: Create the universe-polymorphic tagged well-founded hierarchy required by pm-0002: atoms `q : Q` and arbitrary nonempty indexed nodes, not `Set Q` and not merely finite-depth lists. Define support and the lifted relation by exactly the atom/atom, atom/node existential, node/atom universal, and node/node domination clauses of paper lines 1404-1419. Prove atom reduction, support nonemptiness, reflexivity and transitivity from the base quasi-order, and congruence under extensional changes of node presentation. If raw tree codes rather than a quotient are used, add the mutual-relatedness and invariance theorems that justify them as a presentation of the paper's iterated nonempty powerset.

tasks.title: Reflect bad maps and prove powerset preservation
tasks.body: Carry forward the prior task downstream of `iterated-power-core`. Formalize finite comparison plays and Player-I/Player-II strategies, or an equivalent inductive strategy interface, and prove termination, determinacy, the four-clause characterization, and extraction of a Player-I strategy from `not PowerRel`. Make all choice functions depend canonically on the compared hierarchy values. Formalize the diagonal copying construction of paper lines 1533-1550 and prove a separate reflection theorem: a bad locally constant hierarchy-valued multi-sequence yields a bad locally constant atom-valued multi-sequence, pointwise in the source support. Then state and cover `cor PowerQPresBqo` exactly as `Bqo r -> Bqo (PowerRel r)` under the quasi-order assumptions.

tasks.title: Construct the hereditary converse machinery
tasks.body: Attach to the super/multi bridge and iterated hierarchy. Define recursive hereditary countability and its subtype, prove closure under nonempty countable indexed nodes, induced-relation inheritance of bqo, and `Bqo r -> WellQuasiOrdered r`. Add the correctly oriented front theorem needed for recursion: extensions are recursive-below their proper prefixes; do not use the current `FrontTreeWellFounded` Lean signature as if it had that orientation. Use it to define the paper's `TildeF` on `PrefixTree F`, prove front nodes are atoms, internal successor families are nonempty and countable, and prove every value hereditarily countable. Finally formalize `ConverseGame`: a bad super-sequence gives a bad singleton-indexed sequence of `TildeF` values.

tasks.title: Close both hereditary targets
tasks.body: Carry forward the prior terminal task downstream of `iterated-power-preservation` and `hereditarily-countable-core`. Cover `thm BqoHerCtblWqo` in both directions: forward via full powerset preservation, hereditary-subtype restriction, and bqo-implies-wqo; reverse by converting failure of bqo to a bad super-sequence and applying `ConverseGame`. Then cover `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. Prove wqo implies well-foundedness of the induced strict relation. For the converse, turn any bad hereditary sequence into the countable nonempty tail nodes `A_n`, prove `A_(n+1) <= A_n` and `not (A_n <= A_(n+1))`, and obtain a strict descending chain. Do not invoke a general well-founded-implies-wqo statement.

worker_contract.reviewer_comments: Keep Front, NashWilliams, and SuperNW unchanged; their remaining findings are correspondence, substantiveness, or soundness work rather than a missing paper-target package. Build the next package from paper lines 1254-1292, 1465-1502, and 1613-1662. Add separate paired support nodes for existence and uniqueness of the front member properly prefixing an increasing enumeration on an arbitrary base, extension of a front-valued super-sequence to a locally constant multi-sequence, restriction by right composition, commutation with ShiftMap, and preservation of local constancy. Add the deciding-prefix set and minimal-front construction, with its induced value map. Define the finite-set shift relation and expose both badness transports and the corresponding perfectness restriction/extension facts. Then add the target-covering node for lem:subarr with an explicit quasi-order hypothesis and exactly these three equivalent clauses: Bqo r; every locally constant multi-sequence has a perfect restriction; and every super-sequence on an arbitrary front/base has a perfect restricted sub-super-sequence. Prove all implications, including the NashWilliams shift dichotomy and both directions of the super/multi transports. Preserve arbitrary fronts and bases; do not reduce to fixed-cardinality fronts or to the universal base. New proof-bearing nodes require complete NL proofs with explicit principal noderefs, not SKETCH. Defer the Rado and iterated-powerset targets, and do not use the currently parent-to-child FrontTreeWellFounded relation as the later child-to-parent recursion relation; that orientation issue belongs to the hereditary branch.

issues.description: The claimed preservation is false with the defined restriction: badness at x composed with z compares x composed with z composed with SuccSeq, while the restricted shift compares x composed with SuccSeq composed with z. Reverse the composition convention or weaken/restate the lemma.

The theorem uses the same right-composition map as the proposed subbase restriction, so its perfect restriction conclusion is not the paper's bqo restriction and is false in general. Represent a fixed subbase by left composition with an enumeration of that subbase, or change the type and statement before using this lemma.

The equation h|z(x)=h(x composed with z) is not the increasing-enumeration representation of restricting h to the subbase enumerated by z; that representation fixes z on the left. Correct this definition (and its domain/type) or remove the subbase claim.

The displayed x composed with z map does not restrict a multi-sequence to the infinite subbase enumerated by z; the paper's map is h(z composed with x). Correct the composition orientation and update dependent transport lemmas.

The proof transfers perfectness from BaseRestrict, but that node has the wrong subbase orientation, so the premise does not express the paper's perfect restriction and cannot support the claimed front restriction. Repair BaseRestrict and reprove this transport.

With h|z(x)=h(x composed with z), perfectness of h compares x composed with z composed with SuccSeq, whereas the conclusion compares x composed with SuccSeq composed with z. These differ for noncommuting embeddings; reverse the restriction orientation or restate the result.

The conclusion uses the incorrectly oriented MultiSequenceRestrict, while a perfect sub-front yields the map obtained by composing the subbase enumeration on the left. Fix the restriction representation and then restate this transport.

The stated dichotomy is false for the current right-composition restriction. For equality on {0,1} and h(x)=parity of x(0), every z admits x making the restricted values equal and another making them unequal, so neither perfect nor bad holds. Use the paper's fixed-subbase restriction orientation.

The three-clause paper equivalence is attached to the incorrectly oriented MultiSequenceRestrict/BaseRestrict operations; in particular the bqo clause does not yield the stated perfect restriction. Repair the restriction representation and all dependent transport lemmas before retaining this target node.

request.reviewer_comments: Keep Front, NashWilliams, and SuperNW unchanged; their remaining findings are correspondence, substantiveness, or soundness work rather than a missing paper-target package. Build the next package from paper lines 1254-1292, 1465-1502, and 1613-1662. Add separate paired support nodes for existence and uniqueness of the front member properly prefixing an increasing enumeration on an arbitrary base, extension of a front-valued super-sequence to a locally constant multi-sequence, restriction by right composition, commutation with ShiftMap, and preservation of local constancy. Add the deciding-prefix set and minimal-front construction, with its induced value map. Define the finite-set shift relation and expose both badness transports and the corresponding perfectness restriction/extension facts. Then add the target-covering node for lem:subarr with an explicit quasi-order hypothesis and exactly these three equivalent clauses: Bqo r; every locally constant multi-sequence has a perfect restriction; and every super-sequence on an arbitrary front/base has a perfect restricted sub-super-sequence. Prove all implications, including the NashWilliams shift dichotomy and both directions of the super/multi transports. Preserve arbitrary fronts and bases; do not reduce to fixed-cardinality fronts or to the universal base. New proof-bearing nodes require complete NL proofs with explicit principal noderefs, not SKETCH. Defer the Rado and iterated-powerset targets, and do not use the currently parent-to-child FrontTreeWellFounded relation as the later child-to-parent recursion relation; that orientation issue belongs to the hereditary branch.

request.reviewer_comments: Keep Front, NashWilliams, and SuperNW unchanged; their remaining findings are correspondence, substantiveness, or soundness work rather than a missing paper-target package. Build the next package from paper lines 1254-1292, 1465-1502, and 1613-1662. Add separate paired support nodes for existence and uniqueness of the front member properly prefixing an increasing enumeration on an arbitrary base, extension of a front-valued super-sequence to a locally constant multi-sequence, restriction by right composition, commutation with ShiftMap, and preservation of local constancy. Add the deciding-prefix set and minimal-front construction, with its induced value map. Define the finite-set shift relation and expose both badness transports and the corresponding perfectness restriction/extension facts. Then add the target-covering node for lem:subarr with an explicit quasi-order hypothesis and exactly these three equivalent clauses: Bqo r; every locally constant multi-sequence has a perfect restriction; and every super-sequence on an arbitrary front/base has a perfect restricted sub-super-sequence. Prove all implications, including the NashWilliams shift dichotomy and both directions of the super/multi transports. Preserve arbitrary fronts and bases; do not reduce to fixed-cardinality fronts or to the universal base. New proof-bearing nodes require complete NL proofs with explicit principal noderefs, not SKETCH. Defer the Rado and iterated-powerset targets, and do not use the currently parent-to-child FrontTreeWellFounded relation as the later child-to-parent recursion relation; that orientation issue belongs to the hereditary branch.

The theorem uses the same right-composition map as the proposed subbase restriction, so its perfect restriction conclusion is not the paper's bqo restriction and is false in general. Represent a fixed subbase by left composition with an enumeration of that subbase, or change the type and statement before using this lemma.

The equation h|z(x)=h(x composed with z) is not the increasing-enumeration representation of restricting h to the subbase enumerated by z; that representation fixes z on the left. Correct this definition (and its domain/type) or remove the subbase claim.

The displayed x composed with z map does not restrict a multi-sequence to the infinite subbase enumerated by z; the paper's map is h(z composed with x). Correct the composition orientation and update dependent transport lemmas.

The proof transfers perfectness from BaseRestrict, but that node has the wrong subbase orientation, so the premise does not express the paper's perfect restriction and cannot support the claimed front restriction. Repair BaseRestrict and reprove this transport.

With h|z(x)=h(x composed with z), perfectness of h compares x composed with z composed with SuccSeq, whereas the conclusion compares x composed with SuccSeq composed with z. These differ for noncommuting embeddings; reverse the restriction orientation or restate the result.

The conclusion uses the incorrectly oriented MultiSequenceRestrict, while a perfect sub-front yields the map obtained by composing the subbase enumeration on the left. Fix the restriction representation and then restate this transport.

The stated dichotomy is false for the current right-composition restriction. For equality on {0,1} and h(x)=parity of x(0), every z admits x making the restricted values equal and another making them unequal, so neither perfect nor bad holds. Use the paper's fixed-subbase restriction orientation.

The three-clause paper equivalence is attached to the incorrectly oriented MultiSequenceRestrict/BaseRestrict operations; in particular the bqo clause does not yield the stated perfect restriction. Repair the restriction representation and all dependent transport lemmas before retaining this target node.

v1.summary: Most front, deciding-prefix, shift, and super-sequence definitions and transports are substantive. The restriction layer reverses the composition needed to represent a fixed infinite subbase, making its bad/perfect preservation, dichotomy, and Subarr consequences technically false; those nodes fail substantiveness.
v1.comments: The decisive correction is to distinguish x composed with z (a right action on enumerations) from z composed with x (restriction to the subbase enumerated by z).

request.reviewer_comments: Keep Front, NashWilliams, and SuperNW unchanged; their remaining findings are correspondence, substantiveness, or soundness work rather than a missing paper-target package. Build the next package from paper lines 1254-1292, 1465-1502, and 1613-1662. Add separate paired support nodes for existence and uniqueness of the front member properly prefixing an increasing enumeration on an arbitrary base, extension of a front-valued super-sequence to a locally constant multi-sequence, restriction by right composition, commutation with ShiftMap, and preservation of local constancy. Add the deciding-prefix set and minimal-front construction, with its induced value map. Define the finite-set shift relation and expose both badness transports and the corresponding perfectness restriction/extension facts. Then add the target-covering node for lem:subarr with an explicit quasi-order hypothesis and exactly these three equivalent clauses: Bqo r; every locally constant multi-sequence has a perfect restriction; and every super-sequence on an arbitrary front/base has a perfect restricted sub-super-sequence. Prove all implications, including the NashWilliams shift dichotomy and both directions of the super/multi transports. Preserve arbitrary fronts and bases; do not reduce to fixed-cardinality fronts or to the universal base. New proof-bearing nodes require complete NL proofs with explicit principal noderefs, not SKETCH. Defer the Rado and iterated-powerset targets, and do not use the currently parent-to-child FrontTreeWellFounded relation as the later child-to-parent recursion relation; that orientation issue belongs to the hereditary branch.

issues.description: The claimed preservation is false with the defined restriction: badness at x composed with z compares x composed with z composed with SuccSeq, while the restricted shift compares x composed with SuccSeq composed with z. Reverse the composition convention or weaken/restate the lemma.

The theorem uses the same right-composition map as the proposed subbase restriction, so its perfect restriction conclusion is not the paper's bqo restriction and is false in general. Represent a fixed subbase by left composition with an enumeration of that subbase, or change the type and statement before using this lemma.

The equation h|z(x)=h(x composed with z) is not the increasing-enumeration representation of restricting h to the subbase enumerated by z; that representation fixes z on the left. Correct this definition (and its domain/type) or remove the subbase claim.

The displayed x composed with z map does not restrict a multi-sequence to the infinite subbase enumerated by z; the paper's map is h(z composed with x). Correct the composition orientation and update dependent transport lemmas.

The proof transfers perfectness from BaseRestrict, but that node has the wrong subbase orientation, so the premise does not express the paper's perfect restriction and cannot support the claimed front restriction. Repair BaseRestrict and reprove this transport.

With h|z(x)=h(x composed with z), perfectness of h compares x composed with z composed with SuccSeq, whereas the conclusion compares x composed with SuccSeq composed with z. These differ for noncommuting embeddings; reverse the restriction orientation or restate the result.

The conclusion uses the incorrectly oriented MultiSequenceRestrict, while a perfect sub-front yields the map obtained by composing the subbase enumeration on the left. Fix the restriction representation and then restate this transport.

The stated dichotomy is false for the current right-composition restriction. For equality on {0,1} and h(x)=parity of x(0), every z admits x making the restricted values equal and another making them unequal, so neither perfect nor bad holds. Use the paper's fixed-subbase restriction orientation.

The three-clause paper equivalence is attached to the incorrectly oriented MultiSequenceRestrict/BaseRestrict operations; in particular the bqo clause does not yield the stated perfect restriction. Repair the restriction representation and all dependent transport lemmas before retaining this target node.

stuck_math_audit.trigger: coverage re-planning: 5 configured target(s) with no covering node and 0 covered without a real (non-SKETCH) NL proof — assess the current plan and re-plan the route to full coverage

audit_plan.report:
## Claim being audited

This is the cycle-5 coverage re-plan for the five configured targets that still have no covering node. The first four tasks of the prior plan are complete: the increasing-embedding/local-constancy foundation, generalized-shift reduction and consequences, and the front/Nash-Williams/SuperNW statement package are present. Their configured targets are covered and should not be reconstructed. The current node-level correspondence, substantiveness, and soundness findings on that already-built material are separate verifier work; this coverage plan uses the principal statements and follows the reviewer's instruction not to rewrite them during the next construction burst.

The remaining targets are exactly `lem:subarr`, `lines:985-987`, `cor PowerQPresBqo`, `thm BqoHerCtblWqo`, and `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. The four still-live tasks from the prior plan remain mathematically correct, but they now need sharper attachment points and smaller support packages.

## Existing interfaces and one correction

`IncSeq`, `RightComp`, `ShiftMap`, `LocallyConstant`, `BadMultiSequence`, and `Bqo` provide the multi-sequence side. `Front`, `FrontRestrict`, `SuperSequence`, `NashWilliams`, and `SuperNW` provide the front side. The probe at `.trellis/stuck-math-audit/cycle-5-request-33/right_comp_probe.lean` confirms on the nontrivial embedding `n |-> 2*n` that `ShiftMap x` evaluates as `x (n+1)`, so the existing shift interface can be reused.

There is, however, an orientation issue relevant to the later hereditary-countability construction. The current Lean signature of `FrontTreeWellFounded` makes `u` related to `v` when `u` is a proper initial segment of `v`. In Lean's `WellFounded r` recursion, computing at `s` may call values at `t` when `r t s`; the paper's definition of `TildeF(s)` at lines 1559-1563 calls `TildeF(t)` for strict extensions `t` of `s`. Thus that construction needs the converse relation, `r child parent` iff `parent` is a proper initial segment of `child`. Add a correctly oriented helper for this use; do not pretend the current signature supplies the recursion principle. This does not require changing the already covered Nash-Williams statement during the next burst.

## Remaining DAG

```text
Front + SuperSequence + ProperPrefixSet
  + IncSeq/RightComp + LocallyConstant
    -> unique front selector / super extension
    -> minimal deciding front / multi restriction
    -> finite shift and bad/perfect transports
    + NashWilliams -> shift perfect-or-bad dichotomy -> Subarr

NashWilliams -> constant-k front Ramsey (k=3,4)
  + Rado order + domination on Set Q
  + bad-powerset witness map -> two thinnings -> RadoEmbedding

PowerTree(atom, arbitrary nonempty indexed node)
  -> support + four-clause PowerRel + preorder/extensional invariance
  -> finite comparison strategies and canonical negative moves
  + LocallyConstant/BadMultiSequence -> BadMapReflection
  + Bqo -> PowerQPresBqo

PowerTree + HereditarilyCountable
  + correctly oriented front-extension well-foundedness
  + bad multi-to-super transport -> TildeF -> ConverseGame
  + PowerQPresBqo + Bqo-to-Wqo -> BqoHerCtblWqo
  + countable tail-node construction -> BqoHerCtblWellF
```

For `lem:subarr`, represent a sub-multi-sequence of `h` by precomposition with `RightComp z`. Prove its commutation with `ShiftMap`, preservation of local constancy, and preservation of badness. For a super-sequence on an arbitrary front base `X`, select the unique front member properly prefixing an increasing enumeration whose range lies in `X`; reindex through an increasing enumeration of `X` when a global `MultiSequence` is required. The minimal deciding-front construction of paper lines 1277-1289 then makes the Boolean coloring `r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x))` into a super-sequence. `NashWilliams` yields a restriction on which this coloring is constant, hence a perfect-or-bad dichotomy. The target node must state all three equivalent clauses at paper lines 1652-1658 and prove every implication, including both badness transports and perfectness under restriction.

For `lines:985-987`, use a first-level domination relation on `Set Q`; this is intentionally separate from the iterated hierarchy. Define Rado pairs with `m<n` and the two-clause Rado order. From failure of wqo for domination, choose the bad pair-indexed witness map from paper lines 957-980. Obtain the homogeneous triple and quadruple sets from `NashWilliams` applied to constant-cardinality fronts, as required by process memory pm-0003. The final theorem assumes that `r` is a quasi-order and wqo, and produces a relation embedding of Rado's order into `r`. Its proof must establish both preservation and reflection; the three reflection cases at paper line 993 use badness and transitivity and may not be replaced by monotonicity alone.

For `cor PowerQPresBqo`, retain process memory pm-0002. The carrier must be a universe-polymorphic well-founded tree/preset type with an atom constructor for `Q` and a constructor for an arbitrary nonempty indexed family of earlier trees. Define the lifted relation by all four cases at paper lines 1404-1419, including the often-omitted set-to-atom universal clause. Raw presentations are acceptable only after proving that duplicate/extensional presentations are mutually related and that all predicates used by the targets are invariant under that equivalence. The comparison game, or an equivalent inductively defined negative strategy, must expose the existential Player-I choices supplied by `not PowerRel`. Canonicalize choices as functions of the compared tree values: choosing unrelated strategies separately for each input `x` would not prove that the reflected atom map is locally constant. The reflection node must match lines 1533-1550: every bad locally constant map into the full hierarchy yields a bad locally constant atom-valued map whose value lies in the source support. `PowerQPresBqo` is then the immediate contradiction with `Bqo r`.

For the hereditary targets, define hereditary countability recursively: atoms qualify, and a node qualifies exactly when its index type is countable and every child qualifies. Prove closure under nonempty countable families and induced-subtype inheritance. The reverse direction of `thm BqoHerCtblWqo` uses the bad multi-to-super bridge, the correctly oriented front recursion to build `TildeF`, and the comparison-game copying lemma `ConverseGame`; every internal node of `TildeF` is indexed by a subset of `Nat`, hence is hereditarily countable. The forward direction uses `PowerQPresBqo`, restriction to the hereditary subtype, and the elementary theorem that bqo implies wqo.

Finally, `thm BqoHerCtblWellF` must use the special closure of this hierarchy, not the false general assertion that a well-founded quasi-order is wqo. Wqo implies well-foundedness of the strict part. Conversely, from a bad sequence `(a_n)` in the hereditary hierarchy, form the nonempty countable tail nodes `A_n = {a_k | n <= k}`. Then `A_(n+1) <= A_n`, while `A_n <= A_(n+1)` would compare `a_n` with some later `a_k`, contradicting badness. These tail nodes give a strict descending chain inside the same hereditary hierarchy.

## Work order

Proceed in this order: (1) the super/multi bridge and `Subarr`; (2) constant-arity Ramsey support and the Rado embedding; (3) the iterated hierarchy core and bad-map reflection, then `PowerQPresBqo`; (4) hereditary countability, `TildeF`, and `ConverseGame`; (5) the wqo and well-founded hereditary characterizations. Each helper is its own paired node, dependencies cite principal declarations only, and every new proof-bearing TeX node must contain a complete proof rather than `SKETCH:`.

tasks.title: Build the super/multi bridge
tasks.body: Attach to `Front`, `FrontRestrict`, `SuperSequence`, `ProperPrefixSet`, `IncSeq`, `RightComp`, `ShiftMap`, and `LocallyConstant`. Add separate nodes for existence and uniqueness of the front prefix of an increasing enumeration, extension of a super-sequence to enumerations of its arbitrary base, restriction of a multi-sequence by `RightComp`, commutation of restriction with shift, and preservation of local constancy. Define the deciding-prefix set and prove that its initial-segment-minimal members form the front of paper lines 1277-1289, with the induced value map reconstructing the original multi-sequence. Define the finite-set shift relation from lines 1465-1468. Prove badness transport from multi to deciding super, from super to its extension, and under restriction; also prove the corresponding perfectness restriction/extension facts. Do not specialize fronts to fixed cardinality or silently replace an arbitrary base by `Set.univ`.

tasks.title: Prove the subarr equivalence
tasks.body: Carry forward the prior live task, now downstream of `super-multi-bridge-support`. Define perfect multi-sequences and perfect super-sequences for an arbitrary relation. Prove that `x |-> decide (r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x)))` is locally constant when `h` is, convert it through the deciding front, and apply `NashWilliams` to obtain a restricted multi-sequence that is either perfect or bad. State one target-covering theorem for `lem:subarr` with an explicit quasi-order hypothesis and exactly the three clauses: `Bqo r`; every locally constant multi-sequence has a perfect restriction; every super-sequence on any front/base has a perfect restricted sub-super-sequence. Give complete proofs of all implications, using the badness and perfectness transports rather than only the implication printed at paper lines 1660-1662.

tasks.title: Build Rado and Ramsey support
tasks.body: Attach to `NashWilliams`. Define the carrier of increasing natural pairs, Rado's two-clause partial order, first-level domination on `Set Q`, and relation embeddings. Add the witness-selection equivalence between a bad domination sequence and a bad map on increasing pairs. Prove that the family of `k`-element subsets of an infinite base is a front for positive `k`, then derive the binary homogeneous triple and quadruple lemmas by applying `NashWilliams` to the `k=3` and `k=4` fronts. This is the only Ramsey infrastructure needed; do not start an independent infinite Ramsey development.

tasks.title: Cover the Rado embedding target
tasks.body: Carry forward the prior task downstream of `rado-ramsey-support`. For a relation `r` with an explicit quasi-order structure, assume `WellQuasiOrdered r` and failure of wqo for domination on `Set Q`. Extract the bad pair map, thin first on triples to force `f(i,j) r f(i,k)`, and then on quadruples to force `f(i,j) r f(k,l)` for `i<j<k<l`; rule out the opposite colors using wqo. Reindex the final infinite set by an `IncSeq` and define the Rado map. Prove preservation and all reflection cases from paper line 993, hence injectivity and a genuine relation embedding. The final node alone claims `lines:985-987`.

tasks.title: Define the full iterated hierarchy
tasks.body: Create the universe-polymorphic tagged well-founded hierarchy required by pm-0002: atoms `q : Q` and arbitrary nonempty indexed nodes, not `Set Q` and not merely finite-depth lists. Define support and the lifted relation by exactly the atom/atom, atom/node existential, node/atom universal, and node/node domination clauses of paper lines 1404-1419. Prove atom reduction, support nonemptiness, reflexivity and transitivity from the base quasi-order, and congruence under extensional changes of node presentation. If raw tree codes rather than a quotient are used, add the mutual-relatedness and invariance theorems that justify them as a presentation of the paper's iterated nonempty powerset.

tasks.title: Reflect bad maps and prove powerset preservation
tasks.body: Carry forward the prior task downstream of `iterated-power-core`. Formalize finite comparison plays and Player-I/Player-II strategies, or an equivalent inductive strategy interface, and prove termination, determinacy, the four-clause characterization, and extraction of a Player-I strategy from `not PowerRel`. Make all choice functions depend canonically on the compared hierarchy values. Formalize the diagonal copying construction of paper lines 1533-1550 and prove a separate reflection theorem: a bad locally constant hierarchy-valued multi-sequence yields a bad locally constant atom-valued multi-sequence, pointwise in the source support. Then state and cover `cor PowerQPresBqo` exactly as `Bqo r -> Bqo (PowerRel r)` under the quasi-order assumptions.

tasks.title: Construct the hereditary converse machinery
tasks.body: Attach to the super/multi bridge and iterated hierarchy. Define recursive hereditary countability and its subtype, prove closure under nonempty countable indexed nodes, induced-relation inheritance of bqo, and `Bqo r -> WellQuasiOrdered r`. Add the correctly oriented front theorem needed for recursion: extensions are recursive-below their proper prefixes; do not use the current `FrontTreeWellFounded` Lean signature as if it had that orientation. Use it to define the paper's `TildeF` on `PrefixTree F`, prove front nodes are atoms, internal successor families are nonempty and countable, and prove every value hereditarily countable. Finally formalize `ConverseGame`: a bad super-sequence gives a bad singleton-indexed sequence of `TildeF` values.

tasks.title: Close both hereditary targets
tasks.body: Carry forward the prior terminal task downstream of `iterated-power-preservation` and `hereditarily-countable-core`. Cover `thm BqoHerCtblWqo` in both directions: forward via full powerset preservation, hereditary-subtype restriction, and bqo-implies-wqo; reverse by converting failure of bqo to a bad super-sequence and applying `ConverseGame`. Then cover `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. Prove wqo implies well-foundedness of the induced strict relation. For the converse, turn any bad hereditary sequence into the countable nonempty tail nodes `A_n`, prove `A_(n+1) <= A_n` and `not (A_n <= A_(n+1))`, and obtain a strict descending chain. Do not invoke a general well-founded-implies-wqo statement.

issues.description: The claimed preservation is false with the defined restriction: badness at x composed with z compares x composed with z composed with SuccSeq, while the restricted shift compares x composed with SuccSeq composed with z. Reverse the composition convention or weaken/restate the lemma.

The theorem uses the same right-composition map as the proposed subbase restriction, so its perfect restriction conclusion is not the paper's bqo restriction and is false in general. Represent a fixed subbase by left composition with an enumeration of that subbase, or change the type and statement before using this lemma.

The equation h|z(x)=h(x composed with z) is not the increasing-enumeration representation of restricting h to the subbase enumerated by z; that representation fixes z on the left. Correct this definition (and its domain/type) or remove the subbase claim.

The displayed x composed with z map does not restrict a multi-sequence to the infinite subbase enumerated by z; the paper's map is h(z composed with x). Correct the composition orientation and update dependent transport lemmas.

The proof transfers perfectness from BaseRestrict, but that node has the wrong subbase orientation, so the premise does not express the paper's perfect restriction and cannot support the claimed front restriction. Repair BaseRestrict and reprove this transport.

With h|z(x)=h(x composed with z), perfectness of h compares x composed with z composed with SuccSeq, whereas the conclusion compares x composed with SuccSeq composed with z. These differ for noncommuting embeddings; reverse the restriction orientation or restate the result.

The conclusion uses the incorrectly oriented MultiSequenceRestrict, while a perfect sub-front yields the map obtained by composing the subbase enumeration on the left. Fix the restriction representation and then restate this transport.

The stated dichotomy is false for the current right-composition restriction. For equality on {0,1} and h(x)=parity of x(0), every z admits x making the restricted values equal and another making them unequal, so neither perfect nor bad holds. Use the paper's fixed-subbase restriction orientation.

The three-clause paper equivalence is attached to the incorrectly oriented MultiSequenceRestrict/BaseRestrict operations; in particular the bqo clause does not yield the stated perfect restriction. Repair the restriction representation and all dependent transport lemmas before retaining this target node.

audit_plan.report:
## Claim being audited

This is the cycle-5 coverage re-plan for the five configured targets that still have no covering node. The first four tasks of the prior plan are complete: the increasing-embedding/local-constancy foundation, generalized-shift reduction and consequences, and the front/Nash-Williams/SuperNW statement package are present. Their configured targets are covered and should not be reconstructed. The current node-level correspondence, substantiveness, and soundness findings on that already-built material are separate verifier work; this coverage plan uses the principal statements and follows the reviewer's instruction not to rewrite them during the next construction burst.

The remaining targets are exactly `lem:subarr`, `lines:985-987`, `cor PowerQPresBqo`, `thm BqoHerCtblWqo`, and `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. The four still-live tasks from the prior plan remain mathematically correct, but they now need sharper attachment points and smaller support packages.

## Existing interfaces and one correction

`IncSeq`, `RightComp`, `ShiftMap`, `LocallyConstant`, `BadMultiSequence`, and `Bqo` provide the multi-sequence side. `Front`, `FrontRestrict`, `SuperSequence`, `NashWilliams`, and `SuperNW` provide the front side. The probe at `.trellis/stuck-math-audit/cycle-5-request-33/right_comp_probe.lean` confirms on the nontrivial embedding `n |-> 2*n` that `ShiftMap x` evaluates as `x (n+1)`, so the existing shift interface can be reused.

There is, however, an orientation issue relevant to the later hereditary-countability construction. The current Lean signature of `FrontTreeWellFounded` makes `u` related to `v` when `u` is a proper initial segment of `v`. In Lean's `WellFounded r` recursion, computing at `s` may call values at `t` when `r t s`; the paper's definition of `TildeF(s)` at lines 1559-1563 calls `TildeF(t)` for strict extensions `t` of `s`. Thus that construction needs the converse relation, `r child parent` iff `parent` is a proper initial segment of `child`. Add a correctly oriented helper for this use; do not pretend the current signature supplies the recursion principle. This does not require changing the already covered Nash-Williams statement during the next burst.

## Remaining DAG

```text
Front + SuperSequence + ProperPrefixSet
  + IncSeq/RightComp + LocallyConstant
    -> unique front selector / super extension
    -> minimal deciding front / multi restriction
    -> finite shift and bad/perfect transports
    + NashWilliams -> shift perfect-or-bad dichotomy -> Subarr

NashWilliams -> constant-k front Ramsey (k=3,4)
  + Rado order + domination on Set Q
  + bad-powerset witness map -> two thinnings -> RadoEmbedding

PowerTree(atom, arbitrary nonempty indexed node)
  -> support + four-clause PowerRel + preorder/extensional invariance
  -> finite comparison strategies and canonical negative moves
  + LocallyConstant/BadMultiSequence -> BadMapReflection
  + Bqo -> PowerQPresBqo

PowerTree + HereditarilyCountable
  + correctly oriented front-extension well-foundedness
  + bad multi-to-super transport -> TildeF -> ConverseGame
  + PowerQPresBqo + Bqo-to-Wqo -> BqoHerCtblWqo
  + countable tail-node construction -> BqoHerCtblWellF
```

For `lem:subarr`, represent a sub-multi-sequence of `h` by precomposition with `RightComp z`. Prove its commutation with `ShiftMap`, preservation of local constancy, and preservation of badness. For a super-sequence on an arbitrary front base `X`, select the unique front member properly prefixing an increasing enumeration whose range lies in `X`; reindex through an increasing enumeration of `X` when a global `MultiSequence` is required. The minimal deciding-front construction of paper lines 1277-1289 then makes the Boolean coloring `r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x))` into a super-sequence. `NashWilliams` yields a restriction on which this coloring is constant, hence a perfect-or-bad dichotomy. The target node must state all three equivalent clauses at paper lines 1652-1658 and prove every implication, including both badness transports and perfectness under restriction.

For `lines:985-987`, use a first-level domination relation on `Set Q`; this is intentionally separate from the iterated hierarchy. Define Rado pairs with `m<n` and the two-clause Rado order. previous_audit_plan_snapshot.report:
## Claim being audited

This is the cycle-5 coverage re-plan for the five configured targets that still have no covering node. The first four tasks of the prior plan are complete: the increasing-embedding/local-constancy foundation, generalized-shift reduction and consequences, and the front/Nash-Williams/SuperNW statement package are present. Their configured targets are covered and should not be reconstructed. The current node-level correspondence, substantiveness, and soundness findings on that already-built material are separate verifier work; this coverage plan uses the principal statements and follows the reviewer's instruction not to rewrite them during the next construction burst.

The remaining targets are exactly `lem:subarr`, `lines:985-987`, `cor PowerQPresBqo`, `thm BqoHerCtblWqo`, and `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. The four still-live tasks from the prior plan remain mathematically correct, but they now need sharper attachment points and smaller support packages.

## Existing interfaces and one correction

`IncSeq`, `RightComp`, `ShiftMap`, `LocallyConstant`, `BadMultiSequence`, and `Bqo` provide the multi-sequence side. `Front`, `FrontRestrict`, `SuperSequence`, `NashWilliams`, and `SuperNW` provide the front side. The probe at `.trellis/stuck-math-audit/cycle-5-request-33/right_comp_probe.lean` confirms on the nontrivial embedding `n |-> 2*n` that `ShiftMap x` evaluates as `x (n+1)`, so the existing shift interface can be reused.

There is, however, an orientation issue relevant to the later hereditary-countability construction. The current Lean signature of `FrontTreeWellFounded` makes `u` related to `v` when `u` is a proper initial segment of `v`. In Lean's `WellFounded r` recursion, computing at `s` may call values at `t` when `r t s`; the paper's definition of `TildeF(s)` at lines 1559-1563 calls `TildeF(t)` for strict extensions `t` of `s`. Thus that construction needs the converse relation, `r child parent` iff `parent` is a proper initial segment of `child`. Add a correctly oriented helper for this use; do not pretend the current signature supplies the recursion principle. This does not require changing the already covered Nash-Williams statement during the next burst.

## Remaining DAG

```text
Front + SuperSequence + ProperPrefixSet
  + IncSeq/RightComp + LocallyConstant
    -> unique front selector / super extension
    -> minimal deciding front / multi restriction
    -> finite shift and bad/perfect transports
    + NashWilliams -> shift perfect-or-bad dichotomy -> Subarr

NashWilliams -> constant-k front Ramsey (k=3,4)
  + Rado order + domination on Set Q
  + bad-powerset witness map -> two thinnings -> RadoEmbedding

PowerTree(atom, arbitrary nonempty indexed node)
  -> support + four-clause PowerRel + preorder/extensional invariance
  -> finite comparison strategies and canonical negative moves
  + LocallyConstant/BadMultiSequence -> BadMapReflection
  + Bqo -> PowerQPresBqo

PowerTree + HereditarilyCountable
  + correctly oriented front-extension well-foundedness
  + bad multi-to-super transport -> TildeF -> ConverseGame
  + PowerQPresBqo + Bqo-to-Wqo -> BqoHerCtblWqo
  + countable tail-node construction -> BqoHerCtblWellF
```

For `lem:subarr`, represent a sub-multi-sequence of `h` by precomposition with `RightComp z`. Prove its commutation with `ShiftMap`, preservation of local constancy, and preservation of badness. For a super-sequence on an arbitrary front base `X`, select the unique front member properly prefixing an increasing enumeration whose range lies in `X`; reindex through an increasing enumeration of `X` when a global `MultiSequence` is required. The minimal deciding-front construction of paper lines 1277-1289 then makes the Boolean coloring `r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x))` into a super-sequence. `NashWilliams` yields a restriction on which this coloring is constant, hence a perfect-or-bad dichotomy. The target node must state all three equivalent clauses at paper lines 1652-1658 and prove every implication, including both badness transports and perfectness under restriction.

For `lines:985-987`, use a first-level domination relation on `Set Q`; this is intentionally separate from the iterated hierarchy. Define Rado pairs with `m<n` and the two-clause Rado order. From failure of wqo for domination, choose the bad pair-indexed witness map from paper lines 957-980. Obtain the homogeneous triple and quadruple sets from `NashWilliams` applied to constant-cardinality fronts, as required by process memory pm-0003. The final theorem assumes that `r` is a quasi-order and wqo, and produces a relation embedding of Rado's order into `r`. Its proof must establish both preservation and reflection; the three reflection cases at paper line 993 use badness and transitivity and may not be replaced by monotonicity alone.

For `cor PowerQPresBqo`, retain process memory pm-0002. The carrier must be a universe-polymorphic well-founded tree/preset type with an atom constructor for `Q` and a constructor for an arbitrary nonempty indexed family of earlier trees. Define the lifted relation by all four cases at paper lines 1404-1419, including the often-omitted set-to-atom universal clause. Raw presentations are acceptable only after proving that duplicate/extensional presentations are mutually related and that all predicates used by the targets are invariant under that equivalence. The comparison game, or an equivalent inductively defined negative strategy, must expose the existential Player-I choices supplied by `not PowerRel`. Canonicalize choices as functions of the compared tree values: choosing unrelated strategies separately for each input `x` would not prove that the reflected atom map is locally constant. The reflection node must match lines 1533-1550: every bad locally constant map into the full hierarchy yields a bad locally constant atom-valued map whose value lies in the source support. `PowerQPresBqo` is then the immediate contradiction with `Bqo r`.

For the hereditary targets, define hereditary countability recursively: atoms qualify, and a node qualifies exactly when its index type is countable and every child qualifies. Prove closure under nonempty countable families and induced-subtype inheritance. The reverse direction of `thm BqoHerCtblWqo` uses the bad multi-to-super bridge, the correctly oriented front recursion to build `TildeF`, and the comparison-game copying lemma `ConverseGame`; every internal node of `TildeF` is indexed by a subset of `Nat`, hence is hereditarily countable. The forward direction uses `PowerQPresBqo`, restriction to the hereditary subtype, and the elementary theorem that bqo implies wqo.

Finally, `thm BqoHerCtblWellF` must use the special closure of this hierarchy, not the false general assertion that a well-founded quasi-order is wqo. Wqo implies well-foundedness of the strict part. Conversely, from a bad sequence `(a_n)` in the hereditary hierarchy, form the nonempty countable tail nodes `A_n = {a_k | n <= k}`. Then `A_(n+1) <= A_n`, while `A_n <= A_(n+1)` would compare `a_n` with some later `a_k`, contradicting badness. These tail nodes give a strict descending chain inside the same hereditary hierarchy.

## Work order

Proceed in this order: (1) the super/multi bridge and `Subarr`; (2) constant-arity Ramsey support and the Rado embedding; (3) the iterated hierarchy core and bad-map reflection, then `PowerQPresBqo`; (4) hereditary countability, `TildeF`, and `ConverseGame`; (5) the wqo and well-founded hereditary characterizations. Each helper is its own paired node, dependencies cite principal declarations only, and every new proof-bearing TeX node must contain a complete proof rather than `SKETCH:`.

tasks.title: Build the super/multi bridge
tasks.body: Attach to `Front`, `FrontRestrict`, `SuperSequence`, `ProperPrefixSet`, `IncSeq`, `RightComp`, `ShiftMap`, and `LocallyConstant`. Add separate nodes for existence and uniqueness of the front prefix of an increasing enumeration, extension of a super-sequence to enumerations of its arbitrary base, restriction of a multi-sequence by `RightComp`, commutation of restriction with shift, and preservation of local constancy. Define the deciding-prefix set and prove that its initial-segment-minimal members form the front of paper lines 1277-1289, with the induced value map reconstructing the original multi-sequence. Define the finite-set shift relation from lines 1465-1468. Prove badness transport from multi to deciding super, from super to its extension, and under restriction; also prove the corresponding perfectness restriction/extension facts. Do not specialize fronts to fixed cardinality or silently replace an arbitrary base by `Set.univ`.

tasks.title: Prove the subarr equivalence
tasks.body: Carry forward the prior live task, now downstream of `super-multi-bridge-support`. Define perfect multi-sequences and perfect super-sequences for an arbitrary relation. Prove that `x |-> decide (r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x)))` is locally constant when `h` is, convert it through the deciding front, and apply `NashWilliams` to obtain a restricted multi-sequence that is either perfect or bad. State one target-covering theorem for `lem:subarr` with an explicit quasi-order hypothesis and exactly the three clauses: `Bqo r`; every locally constant multi-sequence has a perfect restriction; every super-sequence on any front/base has a perfect restricted sub-super-sequence. Give complete proofs of all implications, using the badness and perfectness transports rather than only the implication printed at paper lines 1660-1662.

tasks.title: Build Rado and Ramsey support
tasks.body: Attach to `NashWilliams`. Define the carrier of increasing natural pairs, Rado's two-clause partial order, first-level domination on `Set Q`, and relation embeddings. Add the witness-selection equivalence between a bad domination sequence and a bad map on increasing pairs. Prove that the family of `k`-element subsets of an infinite base is a front for positive `k`, then derive the binary homogeneous triple and quadruple lemmas by applying `NashWilliams` to the `k=3` and `k=4` fronts. This is the only Ramsey infrastructure needed; do not start an independent infinite Ramsey development.

tasks.title: Cover the Rado embedding target
tasks.body: Carry forward the prior task downstream of `rado-ramsey-support`. For a relation `r` with an explicit quasi-order structure, assume `WellQuasiOrdered r` and failure of wqo for domination on `Set Q`. Extract the bad pair map, thin first on triples to force `f(i,j) r f(i,k)`, and then on quadruples to force `f(i,j) r f(k,l)` for `i<j<k<l`; rule out the opposite colors using wqo. Reindex the final infinite set by an `IncSeq` and define the Rado map. Prove preservation and all reflection cases from paper line 993, hence injectivity and a genuine relation embedding. The final node alone claims `lines:985-987`.

tasks.title: Define the full iterated hierarchy
tasks.body: Create the universe-polymorphic tagged well-founded hierarchy required by pm-0002: atoms `q : Q` and arbitrary nonempty indexed nodes, not `Set Q` and not merely finite-depth lists. Define support and the lifted relation by exactly the atom/atom, atom/node existential, node/atom universal, and node/node domination clauses of paper lines 1404-1419. Prove atom reduction, support nonemptiness, reflexivity and transitivity from the base quasi-order, and congruence under extensional changes of node presentation. If raw tree codes rather than a quotient are used, add the mutual-relatedness and invariance theorems that justify them as a presentation of the paper's iterated nonempty powerset.

tasks.title: Reflect bad maps and prove powerset preservation
tasks.body: Carry forward the prior task downstream of `iterated-power-core`. Formalize finite comparison plays and Player-I/Player-II strategies, or an equivalent inductive strategy interface, and prove termination, determinacy, the four-clause characterization, and extraction of a Player-I strategy from `not PowerRel`. Make all choice functions depend canonically on the compared hierarchy values. Formalize the diagonal copying construction of paper lines 1533-1550 and prove a separate reflection theorem: a bad locally constant hierarchy-valued multi-sequence yields a bad locally constant atom-valued multi-sequence, pointwise in the source support. Then state and cover `cor PowerQPresBqo` exactly as `Bqo r -> Bqo (PowerRel r)` under the quasi-order assumptions.

tasks.title: Construct the hereditary converse machinery
tasks.body: Attach to the super/multi bridge and iterated hierarchy. Define recursive hereditary countability and its subtype, prove closure under nonempty countable indexed nodes, induced-relation inheritance of bqo, and `Bqo r -> WellQuasiOrdered r`. Add the correctly oriented front theorem needed for recursion: extensions are recursive-below their proper prefixes; do not use the current `FrontTreeWellFounded` Lean signature as if it had that orientation. Use it to define the paper's `TildeF` on `PrefixTree F`, prove front nodes are atoms, internal successor families are nonempty and countable, and prove every value hereditarily countable. Finally formalize `ConverseGame`: a bad super-sequence gives a bad singleton-indexed sequence of `TildeF` values.

tasks.title: Close both hereditary targets
tasks.body: Carry forward the prior terminal task downstream of `iterated-power-preservation` and `hereditarily-countable-core`. Cover `thm BqoHerCtblWqo` in both directions: forward via full powerset preservation, hereditary-subtype restriction, and bqo-implies-wqo; reverse by converting failure of bqo to a bad super-sequence and applying `ConverseGame`. Then cover `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. Prove wqo implies well-foundedness of the induced strict relation. For the converse, turn any bad hereditary sequence into the countable nonempty tail nodes `A_n`, prove `A_(n+1) <= A_n` and `not (A_n <= A_(n+1))`, and obtain a strict descending chain. Do not invoke a general well-founded-implies-wqo statement.

previous_audit_plan_snapshot.report:
## Claim being audited

This is the cycle-5 coverage re-plan for the five configured targets that still have no covering node. The first four tasks of the prior plan are complete: the increasing-embedding/local-constancy foundation, generalized-shift reduction and consequences, and the front/Nash-Williams/SuperNW statement package are present. Their configured targets are covered and should not be reconstructed. The current node-level correspondence, substantiveness, and soundness findings on that already-built material are separate verifier work; this coverage plan uses the principal statements and follows the reviewer's instruction not to rewrite them during the next construction burst.

The remaining targets are exactly `lem:subarr`, `lines:985-987`, `cor PowerQPresBqo`, `thm BqoHerCtblWqo`, and `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. The four still-live tasks from the prior plan remain mathematically correct, but they now need sharper attachment points and smaller support packages.

## Existing interfaces and one correction

`IncSeq`, `RightComp`, `ShiftMap`, `LocallyConstant`, `BadMultiSequence`, and `Bqo` provide the multi-sequence side. `Front`, `FrontRestrict`, `SuperSequence`, `NashWilliams`, and `SuperNW` provide the front side. The probe at `.trellis/stuck-math-audit/cycle-5-request-33/right_comp_probe.lean` confirms on the nontrivial embedding `n |-> 2*n` that `ShiftMap x` evaluates as `x (n+1)`, so the existing shift interface can be reused.

There is, however, an orientation issue relevant to the later hereditary-countability construction. The current Lean signature of `FrontTreeWellFounded` makes `u` related to `v` when `u` is a proper initial segment of `v`. In Lean's `WellFounded r` recursion, computing at `s` may call values at `t` when `r t s`; the paper's definition of `TildeF(s)` at lines 1559-1563 calls `TildeF(t)` for strict extensions `t` of `s`. Thus that construction needs the converse relation, `r child parent` iff `parent` is a proper initial segment of `child`. Add a correctly oriented helper for this use; do not pretend the current signature supplies the recursion principle. This does not require changing the already covered Nash-Williams statement during the next burst.

## Remaining DAG

```text
Front + SuperSequence + ProperPrefixSet
  + IncSeq/RightComp + LocallyConstant
    -> unique front selector / super extension
    -> minimal deciding front / multi restriction
    -> finite shift and bad/perfect transports
    + NashWilliams -> shift perfect-or-bad dichotomy -> Subarr

NashWilliams -> constant-k front Ramsey (k=3,4)
  + Rado order + domination on Set Q
  + bad-powerset witness map -> two thinnings -> RadoEmbedding

PowerTree(atom, arbitrary nonempty indexed node)
  -> support + four-clause PowerRel + preorder/extensional invariance
  -> finite comparison strategies and canonical negative moves
  + LocallyConstant/BadMultiSequence -> BadMapReflection
  + Bqo -> PowerQPresBqo

PowerTree + HereditarilyCountable
  + correctly oriented front-extension well-foundedness
  + bad multi-to-super transport -> TildeF -> ConverseGame
  + PowerQPresBqo + Bqo-to-Wqo -> BqoHerCtblWqo
  + countable tail-node construction -> BqoHerCtblWellF
```

For `lem:subarr`, represent a sub-multi-sequence of `h` by precomposition with `RightComp z`. Prove its commutation with `ShiftMap`, preservation of local constancy, and preservation of badness. For a super-sequence on an arbitrary front base `X`, select the unique front member properly prefixing an increasing enumeration whose range lies in `X`; reindex through an increasing enumeration of `X` when a global `MultiSequence` is required. The minimal deciding-front construction of paper lines 1277-1289 then makes the Boolean coloring `r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x))` into a super-sequence. `NashWilliams` yields a restriction on which this coloring is constant, hence a perfect-or-bad dichotomy. The target node must state all three equivalent clauses at paper lines 1652-1658 and prove every implication, including both badness transports and perfectness under restriction.

For `lines:985-987`, use a first-level domination relation on `Set Q`; this is intentionally separate from the iterated hierarchy. Define Rado pairs with `m<n` and the two-clause Rado order. From failure of wqo for domination, choose the bad pair-indexed witness map from paper lines 957-980. Obtain the homogeneous triple and quadruple sets from `NashWilliams` applied to constant-cardinality fronts, as required by process memory pm-0003. The final theorem assumes that `r` is a quasi-order and wqo, and produces a relation embedding of Rado's order into `r`. Its proof must establish both preservation and reflection; the three reflection cases at paper line 993 use badness and transitivity and may not be replaced by monotonicity alone.

For `cor PowerQPresBqo`, retain process memory pm-0002. The carrier must be a universe-polymorphic well-founded tree/preset type with an atom constructor for `Q` and a constructor for an arbitrary nonempty indexed family of earlier trees. Define the lifted relation by all four cases at paper lines 1404-1419, including the often-omitted set-to-atom universal clause. Raw presentations are acceptable only after proving that duplicate/extensional presentations are mutually related and that all predicates used by the targets are invariant under that equivalence. The comparison game, or an equivalent inductively defined negative strategy, must expose the existential Player-I choices supplied by `not PowerRel`. Canonicalize choices as functions of the compared tree values: choosing unrelated strategies separately for each input `x` would not prove that the reflected atom map is locally constant. The reflection node must match lines 1533-1550: every bad locally constant map into the full hierarchy yields a bad locally constant atom-valued map whose value lies in the source support. `PowerQPresBqo` is then the immediate contradiction with `Bqo r`.

For the hereditary targets, define hereditary countability recursively: atoms qualify, and a node qualifies exactly when its index type is countable and every child qualifies. Prove closure under nonempty countable families and induced-subtype inheritance. The reverse direction of `thm BqoHerCtblWqo` uses the bad multi-to-super bridge, the correctly oriented front recursion to build `TildeF`, and the comparison-game copying lemma `ConverseGame`; every internal node of `TildeF` is indexed by a subset of `Nat`, hence is hereditarily countable. The forward direction uses `PowerQPresBqo`, restriction to the hereditary subtype, and the elementary theorem that bqo implies wqo.

Finally, `thm BqoHerCtblWellF` must use the special closure of this hierarchy, not the false general assertion that a well-founded quasi-order is wqo. Wqo implies well-foundedness of the strict part. Conversely, from a bad sequence `(a_n)` in the hereditary hierarchy, form the nonempty countable tail nodes `A_n = {a_k | n <= k}`. Then `A_(n+1) <= A_n`, while `A_n <= A_(n+1)` would compare `a_n` with some later `a_k`, contradicting badness. These tail nodes give a strict descending chain inside the same hereditary hierarchy.

## Work order

Proceed in this order: (1) the super/multi bridge and `Subarr`; (2) constant-arity Ramsey support and the Rado embedding; (3) the iterated hierarchy core and bad-map reflection, then `PowerQPresBqo`; (4) hereditary countability, `TildeF`, and `ConverseGame`; (5) the wqo and well-founded hereditary characterizations. Each helper is its own paired node, dependencies cite principal declarations only, and every new proof-bearing TeX node must contain a complete proof rather than `SKETCH:`.

Define the deciding-prefix set and prove that its initial-segment-minimal members form the front of paper lines 1277-1289, with the induced value map reconstructing the original multi-sequence. Define the finite-set shift relation from lines 1465-1468. Do not specialize fronts to fixed cardinality or silently replace an arbitrary base by `Set.univ`.
tasks.title: Build the super/multi bridge

tasks.body: Carry forward the prior live task, now downstream of `super-multi-bridge-support`. Define perfect multi-sequences and perfect super-sequences for an arbitrary relation. Prove that `x |-> decide (r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x)))` is locally constant when `h` is, convert it through the deciding front, and apply `NashWilliams` to obtain a restricted multi-sequence that is either perfect or bad. State one target-covering theorem for `lem:subarr` with an explicit quasi-order hypothesis and exactly the three clauses: `Bqo r`; every locally constant multi-sequence has a perfect restriction; every super-sequence on any front/base has a perfect restricted sub-super-sequence. tasks.title: Prove the subarr equivalence

tasks.body: Attach to `NashWilliams`. Define the carrier of increasing natural pairs, Rado's two-clause partial order, first-level domination on `Set Q`, and relation embeddings. Add the witness-selection equivalence between a bad domination sequence and a bad map on increasing pairs. Prove that the family of `k`-element subsets of an infinite base is a front for positive `k`, then derive the binary homogeneous triple and quadruple lemmas by applying `NashWilliams` to the `k=3` and `k=4` fronts. This is the only Ramsey infrastructure needed; do not start an independent infinite Ramsey development.
tasks.title: Build Rado and Ramsey support

tasks.body: Carry forward the prior task downstream of `rado-ramsey-support`. For a relation `r` with an explicit quasi-order structure, assume `WellQuasiOrdered r` and failure of wqo for domination on `Set Q`. Extract the bad pair map, thin first on triples to force `f(i,j) r f(i,k)`, and then on quadruples to force `f(i,j) r f(k,l)` for `i<j<k<l`; rule out the opposite colors using wqo. Reindex the final infinite set by an `IncSeq` and define the Rado map. Prove preservation and all reflection cases from paper line 993, hence injectivity and a genuine relation embedding. The final node alone claims `lines:985-987`.
tasks.title: Cover the Rado embedding target

tasks.body: Create the universe-polymorphic tagged well-founded hierarchy required by pm-0002: atoms `q : Q` and arbitrary nonempty indexed nodes, not `Set Q` and not merely finite-depth lists. Define support and the lifted relation by exactly the atom/atom, atom/node existential, node/atom universal, and node/node domination clauses of paper lines 1404-1419. Prove atom reduction, support nonemptiness, reflexivity and transitivity from the base quasi-order, and congruence under extensional changes of node presentation. If raw tree codes rather than a quotient are used, add the mutual-relatedness and invariance theorems that justify them as a presentation of the paper's iterated nonempty powerset.
tasks.title: Define the full iterated hierarchy

tasks.body: Carry forward the prior task downstream of `iterated-power-core`. Formalize finite comparison plays and Player-I/Player-II strategies, or an equivalent inductive strategy interface, and prove termination, determinacy, the four-clause characterization, and extraction of a Player-I strategy from `not PowerRel`. Make all choice functions depend canonically on the compared hierarchy values. Formalize the diagonal copying construction of paper lines 1533-1550 and prove a separate reflection theorem: a bad locally constant hierarchy-valued multi-sequence yields a bad locally constant atom-valued multi-sequence, pointwise in the source support. Then state and cover `cor PowerQPresBqo` exactly as `Bqo r -> Bqo (PowerRel r)` under the quasi-order assumptions.
tasks.title: Reflect bad maps and prove powerset preservation

tasks.body: Attach to the super/multi bridge and iterated hierarchy. Define recursive hereditary countability and its subtype, prove closure under nonempty countable indexed nodes, induced-relation inheritance of bqo, and `Bqo r -> WellQuasiOrdered r`. Add the correctly oriented front theorem needed for recursion: extensions are recursive-below their proper prefixes; do not use the current `FrontTreeWellFounded` Lean signature as if it had that orientation. Use it to define the paper's `TildeF` on `PrefixTree F`, prove front nodes are atoms, internal successor families are nonempty and countable, and prove every value hereditarily countable. Finally formalize `ConverseGame`: a bad super-sequence gives a bad singleton-indexed sequence of `TildeF` values.
tasks.title: Construct the hereditary converse machinery

tasks.body: Carry forward the prior terminal task downstream of `iterated-power-preservation` and `hereditarily-countable-core`. Cover `thm BqoHerCtblWqo` in both directions: forward via full powerset preservation, hereditary-subtype restriction, and bqo-implies-wqo; reverse by converting failure of bqo to a bad super-sequence and applying `ConverseGame`. Then cover `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. Prove wqo implies well-foundedness of the induced strict relation. For the converse, turn any bad hereditary sequence into the countable nonempty tail nodes `A_n`, prove `A_(n+1) <= A_n` and `not (A_n <= A_(n+1))`, and obtain a strict descending chain. Do not invoke a general well-founded-implies-wqo statement.
tasks.title: Close both hereditary targets
