response.report:
## Claim being audited

The cycle-5 audit prescription to define sub-multi-sequences by `RightComp z` is wrong and must be overturned. It conflates two distinct composition actions which the paper keeps separate. Paper lines 1697-1700 say that the subsets of the fixed set enumerated by `z` are enumerated by `z composed with x`, with `z` fixed on the left and `x` varying on the right. Paper lines 1704-1706 say that shift is instead right composition of the varying enumeration by successor. In the current Tablet convention, `IncSeqComp f g` is `f composed with g`, while `RightComp g f` is `f composed with g`. Consequently the required equations are

```text
ShiftMap x                    = RightComp SuccSeq x = x composed with SuccSeq
correct restriction h z x    = h (IncSeqComp z x)  = h (z composed with x)
current MultiSequenceRestrict = h (RightComp z x)   = h (x composed with z).
```

The compiled probe `.trellis/stuck-math-audit/cycle-6-request-41/composition_orientation.lean` distinguishes the two on noncommuting embeddings. For `z(n)=2*n` and `x(n)=n+1`, `(RightComp z x)(0)=1`, whereas `(IncSeqComp z x)(0)=2`. It also verifies the exact corrected commutation law

```text
IncSeqComp z (ShiftMap x) = ShiftMap (IncSeqComp z x).
```

This orientation is forced semantically: the range of `z composed with x` is contained in the fixed range of `z`; the range of `x composed with z` is instead contained in the varying range of `x` and does not describe a fixed subbase. The earlier probe only checked that `ShiftMap x = x composed with successor`; it did not justify reusing `RightComp z` for subbase restriction.

There is also a direct counterexample to the present `ShiftDichotomy`. Take equality on `{0,1}` and the locally constant map `h(x)=parity(x(0))`. Under the current definition, `(h|z)(x)=parity(x(z(0)))` and `(h|z)(ShiftMap x)=parity(x(z(0)+1))`. For every `z`, the identity embedding makes these parities different, while `x(n)=2*n` makes them equal. Thus no current right-composition restriction is either perfect or bad. This confirms that the problem is mathematical, not merely terminology.

## Structural verdict

The front and shift foundations do not need reconstruction. Keep `IncSeqComp`, `RightComp`, `SuccSeq`, `ShiftMap`, the generalized-shift package, `Front`, `FrontRestrict`, `FrontRestriction`, `SuperSequence`, `SuperSequenceExtension`, `SuperSequenceRestrict`, `FiniteShift`, the deciding-prefix/front/value nodes, `NashWilliams`, `BadMultiToSuper`, `PerfectMultiToSuper`, `BadSuperToBase`, `PerfectSuperToBase`, `BadSuperRestrict`, `PerfectSuperRestrict`, and `NoBadPerfectSuper`. `BaseRightComp` is also a valid operation `x composed with z`; it simply must not be described or used as restriction to the subbase enumerated by `z`.

The false cone must be replaced as a unit: `MultiSequenceRestrict`, `BaseRestrict`, `RestrictionShift`, `RestrictionLocallyConstant`, `BadMultiRestrict`, `PerfectMultiRestrict`, `ShiftDichotomy`, `BaseBqoRestriction`, `PerfectSuperToMulti`, `PerfectBaseToSuper`, and `Subarr`. Some of these nodes state true facts about the current right action, but after the root definition is corrected their signatures or proofs change, and retaining the old statements would preserve the conceptual error. Since this is TheoremStating, repair or delete and recreate these nodes in a single restructure burst; no proof-formalization node-retirement request is legal here.

The dependent arbitrary-base interface should be explicit. A paper-faithful package is:

```text
MultiSequenceRestrict h z : MultiSequence E
  with value at x equal to h (IncSeqComp z x).

BaseRestrict (h : BaseMultiSequence X E) (z : BaseIncSeq X) : MultiSequence E
  with value at x equal to h applied to the subtype enumeration z composed with x.
```

The second parameter must be `BaseIncSeq X`, not an arbitrary `IncSeq`, and the result is most cleanly a global-coordinate multi-sequence. It represents the literal restriction of `h` to the infinite subbase `range z`. Its shift law is the displayed commutation equation, so local constancy and badness/perfectness transports follow for the right reason. If the worker instead chooses a literal dependent codomain `BaseMultiSequence (range z) E`, it must provide the equivalence with this pullback coordinate form and use it consistently; mixing the two presentations is not acceptable.

`ShiftDichotomy` has a second, independent defect in its natural-language proof. It currently colors the deciding front of `h` by comparing a value with an unspecified finite shift. Paper lines 1624-1625 do not do this. They first define the Boolean locally constant map `c_h(x)` recording whether `r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x))`, then form the deciding front of `c_h`, and apply Nash-Williams to the positive subset of that front. The positive and negative homogeneous cases become perfectness and badness only after enumerating the homogeneous subbase and using the corrected restriction/shift equation. The rebuilt statement package needs this Boolean-color layer explicitly; merely flipping the arguments in `MultiSequenceRestrict` leaves the current proof unsound.

Finally, the Lean statement of `Subarr` must express paper line 1656 on arbitrary infinite bases, not only `MultiSequence Q = IncSeq -> Q`. Its middle clause should quantify `X`, a proof that `X` is infinite, and `h : BaseMultiSequence X Q`, and conclude that some `z : BaseIncSeq X` makes `BaseRestrict h z` perfect. The super-sequence clause already carries infinitude through `Front`. A suitable target shape is `Bqo r` equivalent to the conjunction of this arbitrary-base clause and the arbitrary-front clause. Prove `Bqo ->` the base clause by pulling back along an enumeration of `X` and applying the corrected dichotomy; prove the front clause through `SuperSequenceExtension` and the exact subbase `range z`; prove the reverse direction using a bad global multi-sequence, `BadMultiToSuper`, preservation under subfront restriction, and `NoBadPerfectSuper`.

The remaining coverage plan is unchanged only after `Subarr` passes correspondence, substantiveness, and soundness with this interface. The Rado target still belongs downstream of Nash-Williams; the full iterated-powerset and hereditary targets remain governed by process memories pm-0002 through pm-0004. Do not start those packages while the shared restriction interface is false, because the later bad-map and super-sequence transports depend on it.

tasks.body: Run a theorem-stating restructure over the false restriction cone. Keep `RightComp` and `ShiftMap` unchanged. Rewrite `MultiSequenceRestrict h z x` as `h (IncSeqComp z x)`. Rewrite `BaseRestrict` to take `z : BaseIncSeq X` and return the global-coordinate pullback `x |-> h(z composed with x)`; its subtype proof must show `range (z composed with x) subset X`. Update the TeX equations literally. Replace `RestrictionShift` by the commutation equation `IncSeqComp z (ShiftMap x) = ShiftMap (IncSeqComp z x)` or its exact evaluation consequence, and reprove `RestrictionLocallyConstant`. Add a separate base-local-constancy pullback lemma only if `BaseBqoRestriction` needs it. Resolve the existing `BaseMultiSequence` correspondence mismatch by either stating in TeX that the function type is defined for every set and used with an explicit infinitude hypothesis, or by making infinitude part of the interface. The executable acceptance criterion is the rfl law in the audit probe.

tasks.body: Downstream of the corrected interface, restate and prove `BadMultiRestrict` and `PerfectMultiRestrict` using exact shift commutation. Restate `BaseBqoRestriction` with `X.Infinite`, `z : BaseIncSeq X`, and conclusion `PerfectMultiSequence r (BaseRestrict h z)`. Restate `PerfectBaseToSuper` so that the produced subfront is the restriction to `Y = range z`, with `z : BaseIncSeq X`; do not existentially produce an unrelated base. Restate `PerfectSuperToMulti` with the corrected left-fixed restriction, or delete it if the final `Subarr` proof does not use it. Every TeX proof must identify the fixed subbase and the composition equation explicitly. Recheck that no surviving node calls `BaseRightComp X z x` a restriction along `z`.

tasks.title: Rebuild the Boolean shift dichotomy
tasks.body: Replace the present `ShiftDichotomy` proof package with the construction at paper lines 1617-1625. Define, locally or in reusable paired nodes, the Boolean coloring `c_h(x)` which records `r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x))`; prove it locally constant from local constancy of `h` and continuity of shift. Apply `DecidingFront` and `DecidingValue` to `c_h`, not to `h`. Apply `NashWilliams` to the positive subset of that Boolean deciding front, enumerate its homogeneous infinite base by `z`, and use the corrected `MultiSequenceRestrict` plus shift commutation to derive the perfect or bad alternative. The theorem remains valid for an arbitrary relation; do not introduce a quasi-order hypothesis merely to hide the construction.

tasks.title: Restate and verify Subarr
tasks.body: Rewrite `Subarr` to cover `lem:subarr` exactly. Under `[IsPreorder Q r]`, state `Bqo r` equivalent to both: for every infinite `X` and locally constant `h : BaseMultiSequence X Q`, some `z : BaseIncSeq X` makes `BaseRestrict h z` perfect; and every super-sequence on an arbitrary front/base has a perfect restriction to a genuine subfront. Prove all directions using the repaired dichotomy and transports. In particular, `Bqo ->` the base clause must pull back along `InfiniteSetEnumeration`, and the front clause must use `Y = range z`; the reverse implication must use the bad multi-to-super route and the impossibility of a super-sequence being both bad and perfect. Do not claim target coverage until the node passes correspondence, substantiveness, and soundness against paper lines 1652-1662.

tasks.title: Build Rado and Ramsey support
tasks.body: After the repaired `Subarr` package is verified, carry forward the prior Rado task. Attach to `NashWilliams`; define increasing natural pairs, Rado's two-clause order, first-level domination on `Set Q`, relation embeddings, and the bad-witness selection equivalence. Prove constant-cardinality fronts and derive only the homogeneous triple and quadruple lemmas needed at paper lines 988-991. Do not start an independent infinite Ramsey development, in accordance with pm-0003.

tasks.title: Cover the Rado embedding target
tasks.body: Downstream of `rado-ramsey-support`, assume a quasi-order `r`, `WellQuasiOrdered r`, and failure of wqo for domination on `Set Q`. Extract the bad pair map, thin on triples and quadruples as in paper lines 985-993, and rule out the wrong colors using wqo. Reindex the final infinite set and construct a genuine relation embedding of Rado's order, proving preservation, reflection, and injectivity. The final node alone should claim `lines:985-987`.

tasks.title: Define the full iterated hierarchy
tasks.body: Carry forward pm-0002. Build a universe-polymorphic tagged well-founded hierarchy with atoms and arbitrary nonempty indexed nodes. Define support and the lifted relation by all four clauses at paper lines 1404-1419, including the node-to-atom universal clause. Prove support nonemptiness, atom reduction, reflexivity, transitivity, and extensional invariance. If raw tree presentations are used, establish mutual relatedness and invariance under presentation equivalence before any target theorem uses them.

tasks.title: Reflect bad maps and preserve bqo
tasks.body: Downstream of the hierarchy core and the repaired multi-sequence interface, formalize the finite comparison game or an equivalent inductive strategy interface. Prove termination, the four-clause characterization, and extraction of canonical Player-I choices from failure of the lifted relation. Then formalize the diagonal copying argument of paper lines 1533-1550: every bad locally constant hierarchy-valued multi-sequence yields a bad locally constant atom-valued one, pointwise in support. Conclude the exact target `Bqo r -> Bqo (PowerRel r)` for `cor PowerQPresBqo`.

tasks.title: Build and close the hereditary package
tasks.body: After powerset preservation, define hereditary countability recursively and prove closure under nonempty countable nodes plus induced-subtype inheritance. Use the extension-oriented well-founded relation required by pm-0004 to construct `TildeF`; do not use the current opposite-oriented `FrontTreeWellFounded` signature for that recursion. Prove `ConverseGame`, then cover `thm BqoHerCtblWqo` in both directions. Finally cover `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`: wqo gives well-founded strict part, while the converse uses the countable nonempty tail nodes of a bad hereditary sequence to build a strict descending chain. Do not invoke a general well-founded-implies-wqo assertion.

audit_plan.report:
## Claim being audited

The cycle-5 audit prescription to define sub-multi-sequences by `RightComp z` is wrong and must be overturned. It conflates two distinct composition actions which the paper keeps separate. Paper lines 1697-1700 say that the subsets of the fixed set enumerated by `z` are enumerated by `z composed with x`, with `z` fixed on the left and `x` varying on the right. Paper lines 1704-1706 say that shift is instead right composition of the varying enumeration by successor. In the current Tablet convention, `IncSeqComp f g` is `f composed with g`, while `RightComp g f` is `f composed with g`. Consequently the required equations are

```text
ShiftMap x                    = RightComp SuccSeq x = x composed with SuccSeq
correct restriction h z x    = h (IncSeqComp z x)  = h (z composed with x)
current MultiSequenceRestrict = h (RightComp z x)   = h (x composed with z).
```

The compiled probe `.trellis/stuck-math-audit/cycle-6-request-41/composition_orientation.lean` distinguishes the two on noncommuting embeddings. For `z(n)=2*n` and `x(n)=n+1`, `(RightComp z x)(0)=1`, whereas `(IncSeqComp z x)(0)=2`. It also verifies the exact corrected commutation law

```text
IncSeqComp z (ShiftMap x) = ShiftMap (IncSeqComp z x).
```

This orientation is forced semantically: the range of `z composed with x` is contained in the fixed range of `z`; the range of `x composed with z` is instead contained in the varying range of `x` and does not describe a fixed subbase. The earlier probe only checked that `ShiftMap x = x composed with successor`; it did not justify reusing `RightComp z` for subbase restriction.

There is also a direct counterexample to the present `ShiftDichotomy`. Take equality on `{0,1}` and the locally constant map `h(x)=parity(x(0))`. Under the current definition, `(h|z)(x)=parity(x(z(0)))` and `(h|z)(ShiftMap x)=parity(x(z(0)+1))`. For every `z`, the identity embedding makes these parities different, while `x(n)=2*n` makes them equal. Thus no current right-composition restriction is either perfect or bad. This confirms that the problem is mathematical, not merely terminology.

## Structural verdict

The front and shift foundations do not need reconstruction. Keep `IncSeqComp`, `RightComp`, `SuccSeq`, `ShiftMap`, the generalized-shift package, `Front`, `FrontRestrict`, `FrontRestriction`, `SuperSequence`, `SuperSequenceExtension`, `SuperSequenceRestrict`, `FiniteShift`, the deciding-prefix/front/value nodes, `NashWilliams`, `BadMultiToSuper`, `PerfectMultiToSuper`, `BadSuperToBase`, `PerfectSuperToBase`, `BadSuperRestrict`, `PerfectSuperRestrict`, and `NoBadPerfectSuper`. `BaseRightComp` is also a valid operation `x composed with z`; it simply must not be described or used as restriction to the subbase enumerated by `z`.

The false cone must be replaced as a unit: `MultiSequenceRestrict`, `BaseRestrict`, `RestrictionShift`, `RestrictionLocallyConstant`, `BadMultiRestrict`, `PerfectMultiRestrict`, `ShiftDichotomy`, `BaseBqoRestriction`, `PerfectSuperToMulti`, `PerfectBaseToSuper`, and `Subarr`. Some of these nodes state true facts about the current right action, but after the root definition is corrected their signatures or proofs change, and retaining the old statements would preserve the conceptual error. Since this is TheoremStating, repair or delete and recreate these nodes in a single restructure burst; no proof-formalization node-retirement request is legal here.

The dependent arbitrary-base interface should be explicit. A paper-faithful package is:

```text
MultiSequenceRestrict h z : MultiSequence E
  with value at x equal to h (IncSeqComp z x).

BaseRestrict (h : BaseMultiSequence X E) (z : BaseIncSeq X) : MultiSequence E
  with value at x equal to h applied to the subtype enumeration z composed with x.
```

The second parameter must be `BaseIncSeq X`, not an arbitrary `IncSeq`, and the result is most cleanly a global-coordinate multi-sequence. It represents the literal restriction of `h` to the infinite subbase `range z`. Its shift law is the displayed commutation equation, so local constancy and badness/perfectness transports follow for the right reason. If the worker instead chooses a literal dependent codomain `BaseMultiSequence (range z) E`, it must provide the equivalence with this pullback coordinate form and use it consistently; mixing the two presentations is not acceptable.

`ShiftDichotomy` has a second, independent defect in its natural-language proof. It currently colors the deciding front of `h` by comparing a value with an unspecified finite shift. Paper lines 1624-1625 do not do this. They first define the Boolean locally constant map `c_h(x)` recording whether `r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x))`, then form the deciding front of `c_h`, and apply Nash-Williams to the positive subset of that front. The positive and negative homogeneous cases become perfectness and badness only after enumerating the homogeneous subbase and using the corrected restriction/shift equation. audit_plan.report:
## Claim being audited

The cycle-5 audit prescription to define sub-multi-sequences by `RightComp z` is wrong and must be overturned. It conflates two distinct composition actions which the paper keeps separate. Paper lines 1697-1700 say that the subsets of the fixed set enumerated by `z` are enumerated by `z composed with x`, with `z` fixed on the left and `x` varying on the right. Paper lines 1704-1706 say that shift is instead right composition of the varying enumeration by successor. In the current Tablet convention, `IncSeqComp f g` is `f composed with g`, while `RightComp g f` is `f composed with g`. Consequently the required equations are

```text
ShiftMap x                    = RightComp SuccSeq x = x composed with SuccSeq
correct restriction h z x    = h (IncSeqComp z x)  = h (z composed with x)
current MultiSequenceRestrict = h (RightComp z x)   = h (x composed with z).
```

The compiled probe `.trellis/stuck-math-audit/cycle-6-request-41/composition_orientation.lean` distinguishes the two on noncommuting embeddings. For `z(n)=2*n` and `x(n)=n+1`, `(RightComp z x)(0)=1`, whereas `(IncSeqComp z x)(0)=2`. It also verifies the exact corrected commutation law

```text
IncSeqComp z (ShiftMap x) = ShiftMap (IncSeqComp z x).
```

This orientation is forced semantically: the range of `z composed with x` is contained in the fixed range of `z`; the range of `x composed with z` is instead contained in the varying range of `x` and does not describe a fixed subbase. The earlier probe only checked that `ShiftMap x = x composed with successor`; it did not justify reusing `RightComp z` for subbase restriction.

There is also a direct counterexample to the present `ShiftDichotomy`. Take equality on `{0,1}` and the locally constant map `h(x)=parity(x(0))`. Under the current definition, `(h|z)(x)=parity(x(z(0)))` and `(h|z)(ShiftMap x)=parity(x(z(0)+1))`. For every `z`, the identity embedding makes these parities different, while `x(n)=2*n` makes them equal. Thus no current right-composition restriction is either perfect or bad. This confirms that the problem is mathematical, not merely terminology.

The front and shift foundations do not need reconstruction. Keep `IncSeqComp`, `RightComp`, `SuccSeq`, `ShiftMap`, the generalized-shift package, `Front`, `FrontRestrict`, `FrontRestriction`, `SuperSequence`, `SuperSequenceExtension`, `SuperSequenceRestrict`, `FiniteShift`, the deciding-prefix/front/value nodes, `NashWilliams`, `BadMultiToSuper`, `PerfectMultiToSuper`, `BadSuperToBase`, `PerfectSuperToBase`, `BadSuperRestrict`, `PerfectSuperRestrict`, and `NoBadPerfectSuper`. `BaseRightComp` is also a valid operation `x composed with z`; it simply must not be described or used as restriction to the subbase enumerated by `z`.

The false cone must be replaced as a unit: `MultiSequenceRestrict`, `BaseRestrict`, `RestrictionShift`, `RestrictionLocallyConstant`, `BadMultiRestrict`, `PerfectMultiRestrict`, `ShiftDichotomy`, `BaseBqoRestriction`, `PerfectSuperToMulti`, `PerfectBaseToSuper`, and `Subarr`. Some of these nodes state true facts about the current right action, but after the root definition is corrected their signatures or proofs change, and retaining the old statements would preserve the conceptual error. Since this is TheoremStating, repair or delete and recreate these nodes in a single restructure burst; no proof-formalization node-retirement request is legal here.

The dependent arbitrary-base interface should be explicit. A paper-faithful package is:

```text
MultiSequenceRestrict h z : MultiSequence E
  with value at x equal to h (IncSeqComp z x).

BaseRestrict (h : BaseMultiSequence X E) (z : BaseIncSeq X) : MultiSequence E
  with value at x equal to h applied to the subtype enumeration z composed with x.
```

The second parameter must be `BaseIncSeq X`, not an arbitrary `IncSeq`, and the result is most cleanly a global-coordinate multi-sequence. It represents the literal restriction of `h` to the infinite subbase `range z`. Its shift law is the displayed commutation equation, so local constancy and badness/perfectness transports follow for the right reason. If the worker instead chooses a literal dependent codomain `BaseMultiSequence (range z) E`, it must provide the equivalence with this pullback coordinate form and use it consistently; mixing the two presentations is not acceptable.

`ShiftDichotomy` has a second, independent defect in its natural-language proof. It currently colors the deciding front of `h` by comparing a value with an unspecified finite shift. Paper lines 1624-1625 do not do this. They first define the Boolean locally constant map `c_h(x)` recording whether `r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x))`, then form the deciding front of `c_h`, and apply Nash-Williams to the positive subset of that front. The positive and negative homogeneous cases become perfectness and badness only after enumerating the homogeneous subbase and using the corrected restriction/shift equation. The rebuilt statement package needs this Boolean-color layer explicitly; merely flipping the arguments in `MultiSequenceRestrict` leaves the current proof unsound.

Finally, the Lean statement of `Subarr` must express paper line 1656 on arbitrary infinite bases, not only `MultiSequence Q = IncSeq -> Q`. Its middle clause should quantify `X`, a proof that `X` is infinite, and `h : BaseMultiSequence X Q`, and conclude that some `z : BaseIncSeq X` makes `BaseRestrict h z` perfect. The super-sequence clause already carries infinitude through `Front`. A suitable target shape is `Bqo r` equivalent to the conjunction of this arbitrary-base clause and the arbitrary-front clause. Prove `Bqo ->` the base clause by pulling back along an enumeration of `X` and applying the corrected dichotomy; prove the front clause through `SuperSequenceExtension` and the exact subbase `range z`; prove the reverse direction using a bad global multi-sequence, `BadMultiToSuper`, preservation under subfront restriction, and `NoBadPerfectSuper`.

The remaining coverage plan is unchanged only after `Subarr` passes correspondence, substantiveness, and soundness with this interface. The Rado target still belongs downstream of Nash-Williams; the full iterated-powerset and hereditary targets remain governed by process memories pm-0002 through pm-0004. Do not start those packages while the shared restriction interface is false, because the later bad-map and super-sequence transports depend on it.

ops.title: Use increasing embeddings with distinct shift and subbase actions
ops.body: Represent infinite subsets of the naturals and the paper's monoid IIf by strictly increasing embeddings Nat into Nat, and represent continuity into a discrete type by finite-prefix local constancy (paper lines 1264-1271 and 1690-1709). Keep two composition actions distinct. Shift is right composition of the varying enumeration: `ShiftMap x = x composed with SuccSeq`. Restriction to the fixed subbase enumerated by `z` is left-fixed composition: the varying enumeration is `z composed with x`, hence `MultiSequenceRestrict h z x = h (IncSeqComp z x)`. In the Tablet convention `RightComp z x = x composed with z`, so it must not define subbase restriction. The noncommuting witness `z(n)=2*n`, `x(n)=n+1` gives `(RightComp z x)(0)=1` but `(IncSeqComp z x)(0)=2`. For an arbitrary base `X`, the fixed enumeration must have type `BaseIncSeq X`.

ops.title: Form the dichotomy coloring before its deciding front
ops.body: The perfect-or-bad shift dichotomy at paper lines 1617-1625 is obtained from the Boolean locally constant map `c_h(x)` recording whether `r (h x) (h (ShiftMap x))`, followed by the minimal deciding front of `c_h` and Nash-Williams homogeneity. Coloring the deciding front of `h` by comparing its value with an unspecified finite shift is not justified: a member of `F^h` does not canonically determine the shifted member or its value. Any formalization of `ShiftDichotomy` must build the Boolean map first, prove its local constancy, and apply the deciding-front construction to that map.
